title: The sharp logarithmic exponent of r(5,t)
main_claim: There is an absolute constant C such that, for every fixed ε>0 and all large t, t^4/(log t)^{3+ε} ≤ r(5,t) ≤ C t^4/(log t)^3. The lower bound comes from an ordered projective-flag graph on N=⌊q^4 log q⌋ random flags of PG(4,q). The edge rule is: i<j are adjacent iff a_i⊥b_j and a_j not⊥ b_i. The graph is shown to have independence number < q(log q)^{1+η}. The proof compares an entropy lower bound for a selected consistent tuple with an iterated compression argument, driven by a sparse-pair description theorem (Theorem 4.1).

issues.location: Lemma 9.2 (overlap geometry), 'Rich planes in the remaining range' paragraph; Section 10.3 BAD-singleton certificate stages
issues.description: These parts were only spot-checked, not fully re-derived. One is the rich-plane counting (skew quotient lines, the second-moment bound sum d_x^2 ≤ C r^2, and the head/tail split of hyperplane cells). The other is the certificate combinatorics in the p-th moment bound (anchors, new pairs, residual roots with root cancellation q^{-.3h}). No error was found in the steps I did check, but these are the least verified parts of the argument.
issues.evidence: Spot checks that passed: the exponent bookkeeping (e.g. J_hJ_p ≤ q^{13/15}, M/n^{1/3} ≥ e^{37g0/60}, M^2/K ≥ e^{23g0/30}, D0 = O(q^{21/40})); the nondominant counts E ≤ Cq^4/a^2 and Δ ≤ Cq/a^2; the ambient bound Δ_x(t)/B ≤ q^{-1/2+o(1)}; and the root-cost exponent h(v-2)+2r ≤ -.3h. The full logic of the rich-plane incidence bound r ≤ Cnu/M and the BAD dictionary/independence bookkeeping was not re-derived line by line.

coverage:
Read all of the LaTeX (about 3000 lines): introduction, upper bound, flags/entropy, predictor statement, compression-local, compression-tree, predictor setup/geometry/score/completion, and the final conversion.

Checked in detail:
- K5-freeness (the five points are forced to be independent, yet all lie on one hyperplane).
- The entropy lower bound arithmetic: 4σℓ+ηℓlogσ−O(k).
- Rectangle occupancy: Chernoff bound plus a union bound over 6q^25 subspaces.
- The marking scan: popular/poor/expensive counts and the O(qσ) update bound.
- The deficit budget B and the identity B/k = O(Dσ^{-β}).
- The decoupling TC-drop.
- Core-dimension bounds and the low-conflict lemma: open bands give dims r+(6−r) > 5; integer bands force equality and land in a rectangle; the (3,3) case uses the span argument.
- The high-rank elimination (3,3) and rank-4 span growth.
- Level-set loss via mixing, u-monotonicity, and the open-band deletion count.
- The fresh-test lemma, including its Chernoff/variance cap sizes and the domination bound.
- Tree retention and depth sums.
- The cost potential G^+ recursion; Λ' and Δ' bounds; the D-recurrence and the final contradiction.
- Predictor small-set, greedy-list and dimension-reduction steps (the restriction dyad, the √τ hierarchy, the conversion test).
- The rich-line polynomial lemma: parameter inequalities, plane factors, Hessian/flecnode argument in characteristic q > degree, common-line bound.
- Line and overlap counts in dimensions 3 and 4.
- Score second moment: E X_H X_H' formula, u_H bound, and the overall e^{-.6P} bound.
- The z_min/ambient counts and the public-table rejection-sampling costs.
- Final Bertrand conversion: the constant 512 and k ≤ 3t/4.
- The upper bound: occupancy lemma fixed point, sampling lemma expectation 3pn/4, and the s=4,5 recursion.

Less thoroughly checked: the rich-plane paragraph of Lemma 9.2 and the p-th moment certificate stages.
